title: RAG ops lab notes — retrieval, caching, eval
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick personal scratchpad about operational considerations for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in production at Redwood. Focused on tradeoffs: latency vs cost vs freshness vs hallucination control.
- Notes from recent reading (RAG, REALM, DPR) + internal experiments (small-scale).

High-level takeaways (working hypotheses):
1) Retrieval latency dominates tail when we do per-request synchronous retrieval. Persistent cold cache (pre-warmed embed store) helps but has freshness tradeoffs.
2) Prefix-caching (cache top-k docs per user/query cluster) reduces average tokens fed to model and sometimes improves factuality for short answers.
3) Vector index serving cost is non-trivial; there are ops profiles: CPU-only ANN, CPU+AVX, GPU HNSW on GPU memory. Pick based on expected QPS and latency SLO.

Papers / linked ideas to re-check:
- "Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)" (Lewis et al.) — hybrid retrieve+generate baseline. Key: ensemble of DPR + seq2seq. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401)
- "REALM" — pre-training with retrieval; ideas for joint training to reduce hallucination. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08909)
- DPR and faiss/hnsw papers for indexing choices.

Notes from infra experiments (Feb 2026):
- Setup: small cluster: 2x m60-like GPU hosts for gen, 3x CPU nodes for index (faiss flat + HNSW on SSD).
- Workload: 500 users simulated, mixed short Qs and long context expansions. QPS ~ 25 p95.
- Observation: synchronous retrieve (roundtrip ~70-120ms) + model latency (50-200ms) -> p95 end-to-end ~450ms due to queuing and batching.
- If retrieval done async + cached TTL 30s -> p95 drops to ~210ms, but stale doc rate ~8% (measured by divergence from ground-truth in eval set).

Operational patterns to consider: (tradeoffs + suggested defaults)
- Embedding generation locality: generate embeddings at edge (caller) vs server-side. Edge reduces pressure on central embedding API but increases client variance. Default: server-side embed service with sticky pools for high-volume customers.
- Two-phase retrieval: 1) quick cheap ANN (fast but noisy) -> top-50, 2) re-rank full-sim with expensive model / cross-encoder -> top-5. Helps maintain small generator context.
- Prefix caching: store generator prefix for common queries (cluster by hashed prompt template). TTL policy: 10s for time-sensitive content, 5min for docs that change infrequently.

Short experiment ideas (next 2 weeks):
- A/B: synchronous retrieval vs cached-first with background refresh. Metric: p95 latency, factuality error rate on NQ-style prompts.
- Index node sizing: CPU-only HNSW vs GPU index on cuML or FAISS GPU. Measure cost/QPS at 99th percentile latency.
- Eval: prompt-slice tests (legal, medical, product faq) to measure when retrieval helps vs hurts (hallucination injection). Build small test harness.

Prompt / architecture checklist (notes for runbook):
- Always annotate generation output with doc provenance snippets (id + score). If score < threshold, add disclaimer.
- Rate-limit re-ranker calls; use scoring heuristics to skip re-ranking for high-sim cheap candidates.
- Monitoring: token-level traces, retrieval latency histogram, freshness TTL heatmap, fraction of outputs with provenance attached.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How to systematically set TTL per customer/document? Can we infer volatility via change-rate or user-reported freshness SLA?
- Cost model for hybrid index (CPU warm + GPU cold). Where's the sweet spot for mid-range QPS (50-200)?
- Best practices for provenance presentation that doesn't clutter UI but is auditable (structured JSON + human summary).
- Can we do RLHF-style reranking in the loop cheaply? Maybe offline training of re-ranker then cheap online inference.

Quick references to internal artifacts / threads:
- Slack thread (design convo): https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0789ABC/p161234567890
- Draft runbook page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/12345678/RAG+Ops
- WIP infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/456

To-do (actionable, tagged):
- [ ] Build small eval harness for NQ-style factuality + latency (assign: Priya)
- [ ] Prototype cached-first retrieval pipeline with background refresh (assign: me / Owen)
- [ ] Run index sizing bench vs faiss-hnsw + GPU faiss (assign: Noah)
- [ ] Draft runbook section for TTL heuristics and provenance formatting (assign: Owen)

Notes to self: keep these as ephemeral until experiments finish. Share summary with eng-serving-runtime and research-infra once we have initial numbers. Save logs and bench configs under runtimes/pr/456 for reproducibility.

End of scratchpad.
